findings.title: Working-hours check rejects a slot that falls outside any one entry for that day
findings.body:
The `find` returns true, which rejects the slot, as soon as one working-hours entry whose `days` includes the slot's UTC weekday doesn't contain it. The slot should only be rejected when no entry contains it. `getWorkingHours` regularly produces several entries per day: split shifts, plus the overflow piece it pushes with shifted `days` when local hours cross UTC midnight (`packages/lib/availability.ts:92-121`).

Concrete case: an organizer in UTC-8 who works Mon–Fri 9:00–17:00 gets two entries:
- Mon–Fri 1020–1439
- Tue–Sat 0–60

A Tuesday 00:00 UTC slot (Monday 16:00 local) matches the first entry's day, 0 < 1020, so it is dropped. A split schedule (9–12 and 13–17) loses every afternoon slot the same way. Fixed hosts and round-robin hosts both hit this (lines 488-493 and 513-518).

These slots disappear silently. Fix: invert the check so the slot is kept when `workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`.

findings.title: Override check rejects slots in the second time range of a multi-range override
findings.body:
Same pattern as the working-hours check. A date override can hold several ranges for one date: `getUserAvailability` maps each availability row with a `date` into its own `{start,end}` (`packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224`). For a slot inside the second range, the first range on the same date matches the date test, and `slotStartTime.isAfter(range1.end)` returns true. `find` then makes the function return false at line 130, so the valid slot is removed.

Fix: compute whether the slot lies inside some override range for that date (`some(...)`), and reject it only when override ranges exist for the date and none contains it.

findings.title: Override date is matched on its UTC day, not the organizer's day
findings.body: After the shift, `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset)` is the real UTC instant, and the code compares its UTC calendar day with the slot's UTC day. Take an organizer in UTC+10 with an override from 09:00 to 17:00 (23:00 the previous UTC day to 07:00 UTC). The override's UTC day is D-1, so a 03:00 UTC slot on D doesn't match it. `dateOverrideExist` stays false and the slot falls through to the regular working-hours check. If the override was meant to open a day that is normally off, that override slot is rejected. Compare dates in the organizer's time zone, or check the slot against the override's start/end interval directly.

findings.title: `===` between two Dayjs objects is always false
findings.body: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares two freshly created object references, so this is never true. The "override with start == end (unavailable all day)" case is never handled here. A slot starting exactly at the zero-length override's instant passes both later checks and is treated as available. Use `.isSame(...)`.

findings.title: `end` is computed from the slot start, so the slot end is never checked
findings.body: `end` duplicates `start` (both use `slotStartTime`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` only re-tests the start. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end is accepted. Compute `end` from `slotEndTime`, keeping in mind that the end can land on the next UTC day.

findings.title: Shifted override minutes wrap past midnight and put slots on the wrong day
findings.body: `startTime` and `endTime` are taken from `.hour()*60 + .minute()` after the time-zone shift, so they wrap modulo 24h. If the invitee offset pushes the override across midnight, the window breaks. Example: organizer in UTC, override 20:00–23:00, invitee +6 gives 02:00–05:00. That window is still attached to `startOfInviteeDay` of the override's original date (`buildSlots` at line 248), so its slots appear about 24h early. A range that straddles midnight (22:00–02:00) gets `endTime < startTime` and produces no slots. Keep the minute offset relative to the invitee day (allowing values below 0 or of 1440 and above, then splitting), instead of taking the clock hour.

findings.title: New test doesn't exercise the failure modes this change introduces
findings.body: The added case reuses the +5:30 day window (`T18:30Z`) for a +6:00 invitee and a single-range override. No test has a multi-range override, a split or UTC-midnight-crossing working-hours schedule, or a round-robin host. Those are the paths the new `checkIfIsAvailable` logic changes, and it currently breaks them (see findings at lines 106 and 139). Consider adding cases for each.

contracts.action: checkIfIsAvailable now filters slots by per-host date overrides and working hours
contracts.equivalent_path: getSlots in packages/lib/slots.ts builds slots from working hours and overrides by taking the union of time frames (computedLocalAvailability), not by rejecting a slot that misses any single range.
contracts.before_after: Before: only busy times and seats were checked. After: a slot is rejected when any one same-day override range or working-hours entry fails to contain it.
contracts.visible_effect: Booking page loses valid slots for split schedules, multi-range overrides and organizers whose hours cross UTC midnight.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: the slots just don't show up, and no error is raised.

contracts.action: getSlots shifts override minutes by the invitee/organizer offset difference
contracts.equivalent_path: Working hours are converted with getWorkingHours, which splits overflow across days instead of wrapping (packages/lib/availability.ts:101-121).
contracts.before_after: Before: raw UTC hours/minutes were used. After: the shifted clock hour/minute is used, which wraps modulo 24h.
contracts.visible_effect: Override slots can appear on the wrong invitee day, or not at all, when the shift crosses midnight.

contracts.action: dateOverrides carry the host's timeZone into getSlots
contracts.equivalent_path: timeZone comes from getUserAvailability (schedule, then eventType, then user).
contracts.before_after: Overrides now include `timeZone`; the type gains the optional `timeZone?` field.
contracts.visible_effect: Feeds the offset computation in getSlots.
contracts.failure_mode: If timeZone is undefined, `.tz(undefined)` falls back to dayjs's default zone.

summary: The new working-hours and date-override checks in `checkIfIsAvailable` reject a slot as soon as one entry or range for its day fails to contain it, when they should reject only if none does. getWorkingHours routinely returns several entries per day: split shifts, plus the extra piece created when local hours cross UTC midnight (e.g. US time zones). Overrides can also have several ranges. Valid slots disappear silently. The change also has a `===` comparison of Dayjs objects, a duplicated start/end calculation, override dates matched on the UTC day, and wrap-around in the shifted override minutes in getSlots.
